call_contract.stable_key_hash: int32(database, key_data, uint32 key_size); the loaded database is passed as the first argument
call_contract.definition_lookup: pointer(database, signed stable-key hash), followed by the upstream canonical key/hash round-trip
call_contract.construct: pointer(storage, definition, actor full CharacterID, recipient full CharacterID, null extra, initialize_special_data=true)
call_contract.can_send: bool(finalized context, null error output); false is a valid available value
call_contract.auto_accept: definition+0x2580 trigger via 0x334C510(trigger, context+0x08), otherwise strict uint8 0/1 at definition+0x2A48
call_contract.raw_acceptance: int64 pointer(context, int64 output pointer) for intermediary then recipient
call_contract.outer_acceptance: uint8(context, answer_mode=1, flag=0, null, null); only statuses 0..2 publish
call_contract.recipient_kind: 0x28BCEB0(full recipient CharacterID) distinguishes human_pending from ai_final
call_contract.destroy: void(owned context), exactly once after every successful construction

per_sample: resolve database, stable hash and canonical definition afresh
resolve actor and recipient by lower-24-bit slot plus complete signed int32 identity
copy final CanSend, ten signed cost slots and acceptance
destroy and clear the owned context before returning
owned_transaction.sampling: the upstream core runs two complete equal samples inside one outer frame
owned_transaction.cleanup_failure: terminal for the bound adapter state; no second native read is attempted
owned_transaction.pointer_policy: database, definition, character and context pointers are never serialized or retained after the call

unique_next_integration_entry: a later owner may bind this private adapter to the existing application-main paused mailbox without changing its native transaction
